name: C11_FALSE_TWIN_FAMILY_SINGLE_VERTEX_L3_BACKDOOR
fixed_family: G_{r,q}, arbitrary r,q>=1, one selected ordered survivor pair (a_i,b_j), one fixed assignment gamma,delta in {3,4}.

definition.one_L3_backdoor: A residual vertex r is a 1-L3-backdoor if for every kappa in its current list, exact fixation r=kappa plus deterministic propagation either reaches immediate contradiction or every surviving undecided connected component has a globally missing color.

target_claim: In every false-twin blow-up member and for every selected survivor pair/assignment, z is a 1-L3-backdoor.
proof_contract: Before branching on z, every remaining A twin has only fixed neighbor s plus z; every remaining B twin has fixed neighbors t,m plus z.
Fixing z removes z from the undecided graph and propagates its color to all remaining A/B lists.
The remaining undecided graph is independent: every residual A/B vertex is an isolated component.
Each isolated vertex has a current list of size at most 3, hence at least one globally missing color on its singleton component.
If some branch creates an empty list, that branch is immediately infeasible and is also a polynomial terminal.
Therefore every kappa branch is structurally terminal by contradiction or List-3.
nonclaims: Does not prove every authoritative C11 residual component has a 1-L3-backdoor.
Does not prove Pi universally polynomially discoverable.
